summary: MetricBuffer#retrieve_updates returns objects that reference freed Rust memory, causing segmentation faults when Ruby's garbage collector runs concurrently with metric scraping threads.
userImpact: Applications using MetricBuffer crash with segmentation faults when garbage collection runs concurrently with metric scraping.
rootCause: Retrieved objects are thin wrappers around Rust-owned pointers rather than fully copied Ruby objects. When GC runs on another thread and collects native wrappers, the Rust side frees backing memory, causing use-after-free when the scraper thread reads from those pointers.
proposedFix: retrieve_updates should return objects that own their data as Ruby strings/hashes/numbers, not wrappers around Rust pointers that can be invalidated by GC on other threads.
workaround: Disable GC during retrieval and immediate serialization into pure Ruby objects (e.g., JSON serialization), then re-enable GC.
keyQuote: The crash occurs inside `rb_vm_search_method_slowpath`, typically when accessing `update.attributes` or `update.metric.name` — suggesting Ruby is calling a method on an object whose native backing memory has been freed.
